issues.body: In emit_row, `gen_graphs(&map.subject_graphs, ...) == None` returns from the whole row, and `gen_graphs(&pom.graphs, ...) == None` skips the whole predicate-object map. This violates the graph-set union semantics implemented by `graph_union`: if a subject graph map is NULL but a POM graph map generates `<g>`, the POM statement must still be emitted in `<g>`; conversely, if a POM graph map is NULL but the subject graph map generates `<g>`, the statement must still be emitted in `<g>`. The early return/continue silently loses valid quads. The existing `r2rml_default_graph_constant_and_null_graph` test is not a sufficient witness because its NULL POM graph has no subject-side graph to preserve.
issues.fix_hint: Represent graph-map evaluation as both (a) whether graph maps are present and (b) the possibly-empty set of generated graph terms. Union the two possibly-empty sets for each POM statement; emit into every term in the union. Emit in the default graph only when neither position has graph maps, not merely when generated sets are empty. For class/provenance, use only the subject graph-map result and omit them when present subject graph maps all evaluate NULL. Add two real-path tests: NULL subject graph + non-NULL POM graph must preserve the POM quad, and non-NULL subject graph + NULL POM graph must preserve the quad in the subject graph.
issues.title: NULL graph map incorrectly discards graphs generated by the other map

verdict.summary: The named-graph implementation incorrectly treats a NULL result from either side's graph maps as annihilating the entire statement. R2RML forms the target graph set by unioning the graphs generated by the subject map and predicate-object map; an empty result on one side must not discard graphs generated by the other side. The current tests cover union when both sides generate terms and NULL when the other side has no graph, but miss both asymmetric NULL cases.
